final_prompt:
We're planning to add team workspaces to this product, so that multiple users can share and manage resources together instead of each working in an individual account. I need a product requirements document (PRD) that the team can review before any engineering starts. This task is documentation only. Don't change application code, because nothing is approved to build yet.

Before writing, read the repo so the PRD matches what exists. Look in the README, docs/, and the code for the current account, user, auth, permissions, billing, and data-ownership models (for example any src/auth/, models/, or schema files). Note which resources are currently owned by a single user, since those are what a workspace would need to own. Scope this reading to those areas rather than surveying the whole repo.

Then interview me with the AskUserQuestion tool on whatever the repo can't answer and a good PRD depends on. Ask in one batch of at most 6 questions. Likely topics: who the target customers are, whether this is paid-tier only, the roles needed, whether one user can belong to several workspaces, how existing individual accounts migrate, and the success metric. For anything I leave unanswered, proceed with a stated assumption and list it in the PRD's Open Questions section.

Write the PRD to docs/prd-team-workspaces.md (create docs/ only if it doesn't exist). Use these sections in order:
1. Problem and motivation
2. Goals and non-goals
3. Users and key scenarios
4. Requirements, as numbered items marked must-have or later, each testable
5. Roles and permissions, as a table
6. Data model and migration impact, based on what you found in the repo
7. Billing and limits, if applicable
8. Success metrics
9. Risks and open questions
10. Rollout plan

Write in plain, concrete prose. Where a requirement relates to existing code, cite the file path. Keep it to what a reviewer can read in about 10 minutes.

You're done when the file exists with all ten sections filled in, every must-have requirement is testable, and nothing outside docs/ was modified. Finish with a short summary of the PRD and the assumptions you made. Don't commit.
